mainTopic: Year boundaries for tithes, vows, and crops: third-year tithes, vows 'for this year', and the one-third growth rule
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about vegetables picked just before and just after sunset on ערב ראש השנה. The two batches belong to different years, so one may not tithe from one batch for the other. When the second year of the cycle turns into the third, the two batches even get different tithes: מעשר שני for the second year and מעשר עני for the third. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns from 'שנת המעשר' that one of the two usual tithes drops out in the third year. A היקש to נחלה proves that מעשר ראשון never stops. A second ברייתא brings the same rule, where רבי יהודה learns it from 'ובא הלוי' and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns it from the נחלה comparison. Next the גמרא explains 'א׳ תשרי is the new year for vows'. A vow 'for a year' lasts twelve full months, but a vow 'for this year' ends at תשרי, because בנדרים הלך אחר לשון בני אדם. Finally a משנה teaches that תלתן is counted from when it sprouts for seed, and grain and olives from when they reach one-third of their growth. רב אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן proves the one-third rule from the הקהל verse, which calls סוכות of the eighth year 'the שמיטה year'. רבי זירא then begins a question to רב אסי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No tithing from one year's crop for another year's crop
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that vegetables picked after sunset on ערב ראש השנה cannot be tithed together with vegetables picked before sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the sun has set, you may not separate תרומה and tithes from one batch for the other. This is because we never tithe from new-year produce for old-year produce, or from old-year produce for new-year produce.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא about vegetables picked right before and right after sunset on ערב ראש השנה. It rules that you cannot tithe one batch on behalf of the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For vegetables, the tithing year begins on א׳ תשרי, so sunset on ערב ראש השנה is the dividing line. Produce picked before sunset is 'old' (ישן), and produce picked after sunset is 'new' (חדש). The basic rule is that tithes must come from the same year's produce, so the two batches cannot be mixed for tithing.

keyTerms.meaning: Separating תרומה, the portion given to a כהן
Separating tithes (מעשרות)
New: produce of the new year
Old: produce of the previous year
From this one on behalf of that one

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why ראש השנה matters for tithes. It is the line that splits produce into separate tithing years.

phrases.english: Once the sun has set,
phrases.notes: On ערב ראש השנה, when the new year begins.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין וּמְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: one may not separate teruma and tithes from this batch for that batch,
because one may not separate teruma and tithes
neither from the new crop for the old,
nor from the old crop for the new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce from different tithing years cannot be tithed one on behalf of the other, and sunset on ערב ראש השנה is the dividing point for vegetables.

steps.title: Second year moving into third year: different tithes
steps.stepSummary: If the year change is from the second to the third year of the cycle, the old batch gets מעשר שני and the new batch gets מעשר עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the second year was turning into the third year: the second-year produce gets first tithe and second tithe, and the third-year produce gets first tithe and the poor man's tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a special case. When the year turning over is the second year of the cycle becoming the third, the two batches do not even need the same kind of tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In years 1, 2, 4 and 5 of the שמיטה cycle, one separates מעשר ראשון for the לוי and מעשר שני, which is eaten in ירושלים. In years 3 and 6, מעשר עני for the poor takes the place of מעשר שני. So here the year change affects not only which year the produce belongs to, but also which second tithe it receives.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, given to a לוי every year
Second tithe, eaten by the owner in ירושלים
Poor man's tithe, given to the needy
Going into the third year

steps.whatToRemember: In the third year, מעשר ראשון stays and מעשר עני replaces מעשר שני.

phrases.english: If it was the second year going into the third,
the second-year produce gets first tithe and second tithe;
the third-year produce gets first tithe and poor man's tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the year-boundary rule to the change from the second year to the third.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Second-year produce gets מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני, while third-year produce gets מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני.

steps.title: What is the source for the third-year tithes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the third year has מעשר עני instead of מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the third-year rule. This sets up the next step, where a verse will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated the rule without giving a source. The גמרא now wants to know which פסוק teaches that the third year is different.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (derived)? A standard request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that the third year has מעשר עני and not מעשר שני.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: 'the year of the tithe' means only one of the two tithes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'שנת המעשר' as a year with only one of the two usual tithes, so מעשר שני is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The verse says 'When you finish tithing all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe.' This means a year that has only one tithe. How so? First tithe and poor man's tithe, and second tithe is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers with a פסוק from דברים. He reads 'the year of the tithe' to mean a year in which one of the usual two tithes is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls the third year 'שנת המעשר', using the singular. That tells us one of the two regular tithes drops out that year. Since the same passage speaks about giving to the poor, the conclusion is that מעשר עני stands in for מעשר שני, which is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: When you finish tithing (דברים כו:יב)
The year of the tithe
How so? Introduces an explanation
Is cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: 'Only one tithe' does not mean only one tithe is separated in total. It means only one of the two tithes from the other years remains. מעשר ראשון stays, and מעשר עני replaces מעשר שני.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
"When you have finished tithing
all the tithe of your produce
in the third year, the year of the tithe" —

phrases.aramaic: שָׁנָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא מַעֲשֵׂר אֶחָד.
phrases.english: meaning a year that has only one of the tithes.
How so?
First tithe and poor man's tithe are given,
and second tithe is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'שנת המעשר' means a year with only one of the two regular tithes, so מעשר שני is replaced.

steps.title: Maybe first tithe is also cancelled?
steps.stepSummary: The derivation raises a possibility: maybe the verse means that מעשר ראשון is cancelled too, leaving only מעשר עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it means that even first tithe is also cancelled?
steps.whatsHappening: The derivation tests itself by raising another way to read the verse. This sets up the next step, which will reject this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the third year has 'only one tithe', that could mean only one tithe in total, namely מעשר עני. Then מעשר ראשון would also be cancelled. A second verse is needed to rule this out.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only... Introduces an alternative reading
Also

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is not so, but rather
even first tithe is also cancelled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the 'one tithe' reading in step 4 should be understood.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that only מעשר שני is cancelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Only one tithe' could just as well mean that only מעשר עני is left and מעשר ראשון is dropped too.

steps.title: First tithe is compared to an inheritance, which never stops
steps.stepSummary: A verse links מעשר ראשון to the Levites' נחלה. Just as a נחלה is never interrupted, מעשר ראשון is never interrupted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Speak to the Levites and tell them: When you take from the Children of Israel the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance.' The verse compares it to an inheritance. Just as an inheritance has no interruption, so too first tithe has no interruption.
steps.whatsHappening: The derivation rejects the idea that מעשר ראשון stops in the third year. It does this with a היקש from a פסוק in במדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls the לויים' tithe their 'נחלה' (inheritance). A נחלה keeps passing down without a break. By this comparison, מעשר ראשון continues every year, the third year included. So the 'one tithe' that drops out can only be מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; introduces a proof verse
The verse compared it (a היקש)
Inheritance, especially of land
Interruption or break

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר ראשון is given every single year, because a היקש compares it to נחלה, which has no break.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And to the Levites you shall speak and say to them:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִקְחוּ מֵאֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַמַּעֲשֵׂר
phrases.english: When you take from the Children of Israel the tithe
that I have given you from them as your inheritance" —
the verse compares it to an inheritance:
just as an inheritance has no interruption,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן אֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק.
phrases.english: so too first tithe has no interruption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possibility raised in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe מעשר ראשון is also cancelled in the third year.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר ראשון is compared to נחלה, which never stops, so only מעשר שני is cancelled.

steps.title: Another ברייתא teaches the same reading
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא also reads 'כי תכלה לעשר' as a year with one tithe, so מעשר שני is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'When you finish tithing' and so on. This means a year that has only one tithe. How so? First tithe and poor man's tithe, and second tithe is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel ברייתא that makes the same first move as רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of this ברייתא is the same reading of the verse. The difference between the two sources will appear in the next steps, where this ברייתא uses a different verse to prove that מעשר ראשון continues.

keyTerms.meaning: Another ברייתא teaches
And so on (the rest of the verse)

phrases.english: Another baraita teaches:
"When you have finished tithing, etc." —

phrases.aramaic: שָׁנָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא מַעֲשֵׂר אֶחָד.
phrases.english: meaning a year that has only one of the tithes.
How so?
First tithe and poor man's tithe are given,
and second tithe is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel source for the same reading given in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר שני is cancelled in the third year.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא reading 'כי תכלה לעשר'.

steps.title: Might first tithe be cancelled too?
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא raises the same worry: perhaps מעשר ראשון is also cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that even first tithe is also cancelled?
steps.whatsHappening: Like the first source, this ברייתא raises the possibility that מעשר ראשון also stops. This sets up its own proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question as step 5, but inside this ברייתא. Here 'יכול' introduces a possibility that will then be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think; introduces a possibility that will be rejected

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן נָמֵי יִבְטַל?
phrases.english: One might think that even first tithe is also cancelled?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן נָמֵי יִבְטַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possibility about the reading in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מעשר ראשון is also cancelled in the third year.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: whenever the לוי comes, give him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה proves from 'ובא הלוי' that the לוי receives his tithe every year, the third year included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the Levite shall come.' Whenever he comes, give to him. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The second ברייתא answers with a different verse. 'ובא הלוי' shows that the לוי always gets his tithe. The ברייתא ends by naming רבי יהודה as its author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in דברים יד:כט is about the third-year tithe, and it still mentions the לוי coming to receive. So the לוי's share, מעשר ראשון, continues even in the third year. The conclusion matches the first source, but it comes from a different verse than the נחלה comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Levite shall come (דברים יד:כט)
Whenever, at any time
The words of; attributes the teaching to a תנא

steps.whatToRemember: Both sources agree: in the third year מעשר שני is cancelled and מעשר ראשון continues. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns this from 'נחלה', and רבי יהודה learns it from 'ובא הלוי'.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "And the Levite shall come" —
whenever he comes, give to him.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possibility raised in step 8 with a verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ובא הלוי' teaches that the לוי receives his tithe every year, so מעשר ראשון is never cancelled.

steps.title: A different verse proves that the first tithe never stops
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says there is no need for רבי יהודה's proof from 'ובא הלוי'. A verse compares מעשר ראשון to the Levites' נחלה, and a נחלה is never interrupted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: You do not need that proof. The verse says: 'Speak to the Levites and tell them: When you take from the Children of Israel the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance.' The verse compares the tithe to an inheritance. Just as an inheritance never stops, so too מעשר ראשון never stops.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, gives his own proof that the לוי gets מעשר ראשון every year, even in the third year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used the words 'ובא הלוי'. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says that proof is not needed, because there is already an explicit source: the verse that calls the tithe the Levites' 'נחלה' (inheritance). Land you inherit belongs to you all the time, with no break, so the tithe that the verse links to it also has no break.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed. That proof is unnecessary because there is a better source
The verse compared it (a הֶקֵּשׁ, a comparison drawn from two things placed together in a verse)
Inheritance or hereditary portion
An interruption or break

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same verse and the same comparison used in the first ברייתא (step 6). Here it appears again, this time inside the second ברייתא, as רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's alternative to רבי יהודה's proof. It is not a new topic.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that only מעשר שני is replaced by מעשר עני in the third year. מעשר ראשון for the לוי continues every year. רבי יהודה learns this from 'ובא הלוי', and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns it from the comparison to a נחלה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
It is not necessary (to learn it from there),
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהודה's proof from 'ובא הלוי' is not needed.

phrases.english: for behold, it says:
"And to the Levites you shall speak
and say to them:
When you take from the Children of Israel
the tithe that I have given you
from them as your inheritance",
the verse compared it to an inheritance:
just as an inheritance has no interruption,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן אֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק.
phrases.english: so too the first tithe has no interruption.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same conclusion that רבי יהודה proved in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do we know that מעשר ראשון is not cancelled in the third year (the question from step 8)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse calls the tithe the Levites' נחלה. A נחלה has no break, so מעשר ראשון has no break.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the proof from 'ובא הלוי' is not needed. The היקש of מעשר ראשון to נחלה already shows that מעשר ראשון has no break, even in the third year.

steps.title: A vow for 'a year' lasts twelve full months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next item in the ברייתא, that א׳ תשרי is the new year for vows. A ברייתא rules that someone forbidden by a vow to benefit from another person 'for a year' counts twelve months from the day of the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for vows', and so on. The Rabbis taught: If someone is forbidden by a vow to get any benefit from his friend for a year, he counts twelve months, from that day to the same day next year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, א׳ תשרי as the new year for נדרים, and brings a ברייתא. This first ruling is the basic case, and it sets up the next case, where the year ends at תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person just said 'for a year', he means a full year of time. So the count starts on the day of the vow and runs twelve months, no matter when תשרי falls. In this case א׳ תשרי makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Vows
A person forbidden by a vow from getting benefit
The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
From day to day. From the date of the vow to the same date a year later

steps.confusionAlert: This case does NOT use א׳ תשרי. Only the next case, where he says 'this year', is tied to תשרי.

phrases.english: "And for vows", etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא brought earlier: א׳ תשרי is the new year for vows.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who is forbidden by a vow to benefit from his fellow for a year
counts twelve months
from day to day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tithe discussion and begins the next item in the ברייתא, vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow 'for a year' lasts twelve full months from the day it was made.

steps.title: A vow for 'this year' ends when תשרי arrives
steps.stepSummary: If he vowed 'for this year', the vow ends on א׳ תשרי. Even if he made the vow on כ״ט אלול, one day before, the year counts as finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said 'for this year', then even if he only made the vow on the 29th of אלול, once the first day of תשרי arrives, the year is counted as complete for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second case. Saying 'this year' means the calendar year, so the vow ends when the new year begins on א׳ תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This year' points to the current calendar year, not to twelve months of time. The calendar year for vows ends at א׳ תשרי, so the vow can end after just one day. This is exactly where 'א׳ תשרי is the new year for vows' has a practical effect.

keyTerms.meaning: For this (calendar) year
It is counted for him as a year
The last month before תשרי

steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows the practical effect of the rule that א׳ תשרי is the new year for vows.

phrases.english: But if he said "for this year,"
even if he took (the vow) only
on the twenty-ninth of Elul,
once the first day of Tishrei has arrived,
it is counted for him as a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 11. Saying 'this year' rather than 'a year' changes the end point to א׳ תשרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow 'for this year' expires on א׳ תשרי, even if it was made one day earlier.

steps.title: Why one day is enough even for those who say one day is not a year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ruling holds even according to the opinion that one day of a year does not count as a year. In a vow, the person only took on suffering, and he has already suffered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ruling is true even according to the one who says that one day in a year is not considered a year. Here he accepted upon himself to cause himself discomfort, and he has already had that discomfort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible objection to step 12. Someone could say one day should not count as a year, so the גמרא explains why it does count for vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In other areas, some hold that a single day is not counted as a whole year. With a vow, though, the point was only to cause himself some discomfort by denying himself benefit. He did that, even if only for one day, so his vow is fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
Is not considered a year
To cause himself distress or discomfort
He suffered or was distressed

phrases.english: Even according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם אֶחָד בַּשָּׁנָה אֵינוֹ חָשׁוּב שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: one day in a year is not considered a year,
(here) he took upon himself to cause himself distress,
and he has in fact been distressed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יוֹם אֶחָד בַּשָּׁנָה אֵינוֹ חָשׁוּב שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the ruling of step 12 against an objection that was never stated out loud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one day before תשרי counts as a full year for a vow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a single day cannot count as a year, according to the opinion that one day in a year is not a year.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vow's purpose is self-denial, and that has already happened, so the vow is fulfilled.

steps.title: Why not count the year from ניסן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the vow's year ends at תשרי. Perhaps it should end at ניסן, which is also a new year.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the year ends at ניסן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of תשרי as the end of 'this year' for vows. This question sets up the answer in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ניסן is the new year for kings and festivals, so 'this year' could just as easily mean the year that ends in ניסן. Then a vow made in אלול would not end in תשרי but would continue until ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us say (introduces a challenge)
The spring month, the new year for kings and festivals

phrases.english: But say Nisan!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in step 12 that the year for vows ends at תשרי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the year for vows starts at א׳ תשרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ניסן is also a legal new year in the תורה, so why should 'this year' end at תשרי and not at ניסן?

steps.title: Vows follow how ordinary people speak
steps.stepSummary: With vows, we go by the everyday meaning of words. Ordinary people count the year from תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: With vows, follow the way people normally speak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about ניסן. A vow means whatever its words mean in common speech, and people count the year from תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's technical new years do not decide what a person meant by his vow. What matters is how people normally use the word 'year', and in common speech the year turns over at תשרי. So 'this year' ends at א׳ תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: Follow, go according to
The ordinary language of people, everyday usage

steps.whatToRemember: A vow 'for a year' lasts twelve full months. A vow 'for this year' ends at א׳ תשרי, because with vows we follow ordinary speech (לשון בני אדם), and people count the year from תשרי.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'בנדרים הלך אחר לשון בני אדם' is a basic rule of the laws of vows and is used throughout מסכת נדרים.

phrases.aramaic: בִּנְדָרִים הַלֵּךְ אַחַר לְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: With vows, follow the language of people.
phrases.notes: This is a well-known general rule for interpreting vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּנְדָרִים הַלֵּךְ אַחַר לְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a general rule of interpretation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe 'this year' ends at ניסן, since ניסן is also a new year in the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Vows are understood by everyday speech, and in everyday speech the year begins at תשרי.

steps.title: A משנה: when fenugreek, grain, and olives become obligated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in מעשרות. It says תלתן is obligated from when it sprouts, and grain and olives from when they reach one-third of their growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: fenugreek is obligated from when it sprouts. Grain and olives are obligated from when they reach one-third of their growth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a משנה from מסכת מעשרות, about the point in growth when a crop counts. It is setting up two questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that תשרי is the new year for crops, so we need to know which year a crop belongs to. This משנה gives the answer: it depends on a specific growth stage. For תלתן that stage is sprouting, and for grain and olives it is reaching one-third.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, meaning a משנה from a different מסכת
Fenugreek, a legume-like plant
Grain
One-third of full growth

phrases.english: We learned there (in a Mishnah):
Fenugreek: from when it sprouts,
grain and olives:
from when they reach one-third (of their growth).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of vows and brings a משנה about the growth stage at which a crop counts, which connects to the new year for produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלתן counts from sprouting. Grain and olives count from reaching one-third of growth.

steps.title: What does 'sprouts' mean for fenugreek?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'from when it sprouts' for תלתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'from when it sprouts' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about one word in the משנה. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תלתן starts sprouting almost right after it is planted. If 'sprouts' meant ordinary sprouting, the rule would be strange and almost meaningless. So the גמרא wants to know which kind of sprouting is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: What, introducing a request for clarification

phrases.english: What is 'from when it sprouts'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the first part of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which stage of growth the word 'sprouts' refers to for תלתן.

steps.title: It means sprouting for seed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'sprouts' means the stage when the seeds are developed enough to grow a new plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when it sprouts for seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word: 'sprouts' means the point where the תלתן's seeds are good enough to be planted again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a later and more meaningful stage of growth, not the first green shoots. It works like the 'one-third' stage for grain: the point where the crop is mature enough to count.

keyTerms.meaning: Seeds, here meaning seeds able to grow a new crop

phrases.english: From when it sprouts for seed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of 'sprouts'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Sprouts' means the stage when its seeds can grow into a new crop.

steps.title: What is the source for the one-third rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second part of the משנה and asks where we learn that grain and olives go by one-third of their growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grain and olives count from when they reach one-third. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second part of the משנה and asks for its source. It is setting up a derivation from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one-third stage is a specific rule. The גמרא wants a source in the תורה showing that a crop's year is set by this stage, and not by when it is planted or harvested.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words learned? A request for a source

phrases.english: Grain and olives
(are obligated) from when they reach one-third.
From where are these matters (learned)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first part of the משנה (תלתן) to the second part (grain and olives).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that grain and olives are judged by the one-third stage.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן brings the verse about סוכות of the שמיטה year
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי, quoting רבי יוחנן (and some say רבי יוסי הגלילי), brings the פסוק about הקהל: at the end of seven years, at the time of the שמיטה year, on סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and some trace it to רבי יוסי הגלילי: The verse says, 'At the end of seven years, at the time of the שמיטה year, on the festival of סוכות.'
steps.whatsHappening: An answer begins: a פסוק is brought as the source. The גמרא is setting up a close reading of its wording, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is about מצות הקהל, the gathering where the king reads the תורה to the people. The important detail is that it links 'the שמיטה year' with סוכות. That link is what will be examined.

keyTerms.meaning: And some traced it to the name of, meaning the statement is also attributed to an earlier source
The verse says
The seventh year, when the land rests
The festival of סוכות, the time of הקהל

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָטוּ בָּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי,
phrases.english: and some traced it to the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
The verse states:
'At the end of seven years,
at the time of the year of release,
on the festival of Sukkos.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the request for a source by quoting a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that crops are judged by the one-third stage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים לא:י, the פסוק of הקהל linking the שמיטה year with סוכות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק of הקהל (דברים לא:י), which links 'the שמיטה year' with סוכות. Its wording is examined in the next two steps.

steps.title: But סוכות is already in the eighth year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק links the שמיטה year with סוכות. סוכות comes after ראש השנה, so it is already in the eighth year.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the שמיטה year have to do with סוכות? It is already the eighth year!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a puzzle in the wording of the פסוק. This puzzle sets up the lesson that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year changes on א׳ תשרי, and סוכות comes two weeks later. So the סוכות right after שמיטה is really in the eighth year. Calling it 'the שמיטה year' seems wrong, which tells us the פסוק must be teaching something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its business here? Why is it mentioned?
The eighth year, the year after שמיטה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real attack on the פסוק. The גמרא asks this question on purpose, so that the odd wording leads to a hidden teaching.

phrases.english: The Shemitah year, what is it doing
on the festival of Sukkos?
It is (already) the eighth year!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה מַאי עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ בְּחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק's phrase linking 'the שמיטה year' with סוכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סוכות falls after ראש השנה, in the eighth year, so calling it the שמיטה year seems inaccurate.

steps.title: Grain that reached one-third in שמיטה keeps שמיטה laws in the eighth year
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that grain which reached one-third before ראש השנה of שביעית is still treated as שביעית produce in the eighth year. This is the source for the one-third rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is telling you: any grain that reached one-third in the seventh year before ראש השנה, you treat it with the laws of שביעית even in the eighth year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the odd wording of the פסוק. In doing so, it finishes answering where the one-third rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'שמיטה year' can still be present on סוכות of the eighth year only if some שביעית law continues then. That law is the produce: grain harvested around סוכות of the eighth year had already reached one-third during שביעית. So the one-third stage decides which year the crop belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it comes to tell you, introducing the hidden teaching
The seventh year, the שמיטה year
The rules and holiness of שביעית produce

steps.whatToRemember: Grain and olives belong to the year in which they reached one-third of their growth. This is learned from the פסוק that calls סוכות of the eighth year 'the שמיטה year', because grain that reached one-third in שביעית still keeps שביעית laws then.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets the year for grain and olives, for שביעית and also for מעשרות. That is why their year is judged by the one-third stage and not by when they are harvested. Other produce works differently: for vegetables, step 1 showed that the year is set by when they are picked.

phrases.english: Rather, (it comes) to tell you:
any grain that reached one-third
in the seventh year, before Rosh Hashanah,
you treat it with the laws of the seventh year
in the eighth year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the odd wording raised in the previous step and uses it to finish the source for the one-third rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of an odd phrase as carrying a hidden law (a דרשה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'שמיטה year' on סוכות seemed inaccurate, since סוכות is in the eighth year.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase teaches that grain which reached one-third in שביעית keeps שביעית laws into the eighth year, which proves that the one-third stage sets a crop's year.

steps.title: רבי זירא turns to רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא begins speaking to רב אסי. This line only introduces him; his actual question comes in the next words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב אסי:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that רבי זירא is about to respond to רב אסי, and the next words will hold his actual point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי just gave the פסוק source for the one-third rule. Now רבי זירא, a student-colleague, speaks to him directly, which signals that the rule is about to be questioned or clarified. Nothing new is said yet; only the speaker and the listener are named.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him. This phrase opens a direct reply or question to a specific person.
An אמורא who often asks sharp questions of his teachers and colleagues.
The אמורא who brought the פסוק source for the one-third rule in Step 20.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a new law in this line. It is only the opening of רבי זירא's question. The content comes in the next part of the text.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Asi:
phrases.notes: This attribution line opens רבי זירא's question to רב אסי about the one-third rule, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אסי's source for the one-third rule is settled, רבי זירא turns to רב אסי himself to question or clarify that rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not stated yet. This line only introduces רבי זירא's coming question to רב אסי about the one-third rule.
